D.treatment: data-driven assessment using time to complete the task

O.outcome_detail: use of time to complete as the main assessment parameter

cells.quote: The results show that, to date, 98% of the studies that used data-driven assessment tools in clinical practice, also used time to complete a training task as the main parameter for efficiency and technical competency.
cells.note: This is a descriptive prevalence finding, not evidence that time-based assessment improved performance relative to other parameters.

result.effect: 32 of 35 studies (91%) assessed instrument handling; 8 studies (20%) assessed tissue handling or integrity

cells.quote:
Thirty-two (91%) of the studies reported on instrument handling skills, most often presented as path length, speed, or smoothness, with units varying between studies.

Eight studies (20%) reported on tissue handling assessment or tissue integrity, presented as- suture integrity: breaking strength30,31 or knot loosening.30,32.
cells.note: The review reports frequency of assessment domains rather than a controlled learning-effect comparison.

D.comparison: data-driven assessment used in experiments or validation studies

O.outcome_detail: adoption and implementation in laparoscopic skills training

result.effect: 35 included curriculum studies versus 174 studies reporting tools mainly in experiments or validation studies

cells.quote:
A total of 174 studies (24%) reported on data-driven assessment tools, but mainly in experiments and validation studies, and not adopted into a skills training curriculum for surgical residents.

The full-text screening resulted in 35 studies (5%) that were included (Figure 1).
cells.note: The comparison concerns implementation context, not learner performance.

result.effect: 24 studies reported previously established validity evidence; 11 studies used tools that were not validated

cells.quote: Eleven (31%) studies used a data-driven assessment tool that was not validated. The remaining 24 studies reported on assessment tools with previously established validity evidence, with a total of 55 references to the literature.
cells.note: This codes the review's reporting of validity evidence, not a direct comparison of assessment accuracy.
